subject: OPEN statement
notes: CONFORMS, and RE-DECIDED without a change of verdict (kb/Work PB802, owner decision 2026-09-07 verbatim: 'Let's match GNUCobol's implementation in spirit. No sidecar of any type.'; it supersedes the catalog PB193 landed). GR10's comparison still runs on FileConnector.Open BEFORE OpenCore (GR25 leaves an unsuccessful OPEN's file unaffected and the creation arms truncate), still returns FileStatusCode.FixedAttributeConflict '39' (9.1.13.6 item 7), and both OPEN dispatch arms still reach it (the plain registry Open and the sharing-active SharedOpenAttempt). WHAT CHANGED IS WHERE THE FILE'S ATTRIBUTES COME FROM: there is no catalog and no sidecar of any type (NTFS alternate data streams were considered and rejected with it), so a physical file's 9.1.6 fixed file attributes are whatever ITS OWN BYTES record. THE VALIDATED SET IS THEREFORE A RULE RATHER THAN A TABLE - exactly what each organization's format encodes - realized as three overrides of ONE virtual, FileConnector.FixedAttributeConflict, each beside the format it reads, so an organization added later brings its own answer instead of needing a row in a switch (the hand-kept MediumFixesRecordLayout classification is deleted). (1) Fixed-length record sequential and line sequential encode NOTHING, so nothing is validated - 9.1.7.2 puts those lengths in the data and in the reading program, and 9.1.13.2 items 3, 5 and 7 answer the disagreement with the SUCCESSFUL '04', '06' and '09'; a uniform set was MEASURED WRONG in 2026-08 (six conforming corpus programs red, one into an infinite READ loop). (2) A RECORD VARYING record-sequential file encodes its record type in 9.1.7.2's own 'record length headers' - WiseOwl COBOL's 4-byte little-endian prefix, by the method 12.4.5.11.4 GR5 leaves to the implementor - so a first prefix naming more bytes than the file holds is not a framed file and the declared VARIABLE record type contradicts the medium: '39'. A prefix that PARSES but falls outside the RECORD clause's bounds is NOT a conflict; that is item 3's '04' on the READ, which a '39' at the OPEN would make unreachable (golden step 16 pins exactly that boundary). (3) RELATIVE and INDEXED encode the organization, record type, minimum and maximum logical record size and the key table in the framed store's HEADER, which is IN the data file as GnuCOBOL's ISAM key definitions are; a store with no readable header is '39' (loud) rather than a silent misread, and a zero-byte file is the one tolerated exception. The key check has a documented runtime opt-out, WISEOWL_COBOL_KEYCHECK=OFF (GnuCOBOL's COB_KEYCHECK), read once per run unit and registered in RuntimeConfig. HONEST COST, PINNED AS A DECISION: PB193's original probe - a RELATIVE file reopened INPUT through a SEQUENTIAL or LINE SEQUENTIAL FD - no longer answers '39' but '00' (golden step 3, with its READ and its comment), because a sequential file's format states nothing for the store to contradict; the reverse direction still answers '39' (golden step 13) and RecordLayoutNotice still reports the byte-count disagreement on stderr. Surveyed, not assumed: GnuCOBOL's testsuite has exactly two status-39 cases, 'variable-length SEQUENTIAL data integrity' and 'INDEXED undeclared keys' with its COB_KEYCHECK=OFF opt-out, and both are reproduced.
